hints: Focus on what makes a free radical special, it is simply a species with one or more unpaired electrons.
Count the total electrons in each species: $\text{He}$ has 2, $\text{Be}^-$ has 5, $\text{O}^{2-}$ has 10, and $\text{Zn}$ has 30.
Remember that a species with an odd number of electrons cannot have all electrons paired, so it must be the radical.
walkthrough:
**Recall the definition of a free radical**

A free radical is any atom, molecule or ion with at least one unpaired electron. It does not have to be neutral, it just needs that lonely electron.

Rule to use:
$$\text{odd number of electrons} \rightarrow \text{must have an unpaired electron}$$

**Count electrons for each species**

Let's find the total electrons from atomic number minus charge (add electrons for negative charge).

$$\text{He: } 2 - 0 = 2 \text{ electrons}$$
$$\text{Be}^-: 4 - (-1) = 5 \text{ electrons}$$
$$\text{O}^{2-}: 8 - (-2) = 10 \text{ electrons}$$
$$\text{Zn: } 30 - 0 = 30 \text{ electrons}$$

**Check pairing with electron configurations**

Only the species with 5 electrons must leave one unpaired.

$$\text{He: } 1s^2 \text{ (paired)}$$
$$\text{Be}^-: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^1 \text{ (one unpaired in 2p)}$$
$$\text{O}^{2-}: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 \text{ (full octet, all paired)}$$
$$\text{Zn: } [\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^2 \text{ (all paired)}$$

**Pick the radical**

$\text{Be}^-$ is the only one with an odd electron count and an unpaired electron, so it is the free radical.

options.A: He has configuration $1s^2$. Both electrons are paired in the full 1s shell, so it is very stable and definitely not a radical.
options.B: Neutral Be is $1s^2 2s^2$. Adding one electron gives $\text{Be}^-$ as $1s^2 2s^2 2p^1$. With 5 electrons total, the last electron in 2p is unpaired, so this is a free radical.
options.C: O has 8 electrons ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^4$). Adding 2 electrons gives $\text{O}^{2-}$ as $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6$, a full stable octet like neon. All electrons are paired, so it is not a radical.
options.D: Zn is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^{10} 4s^2$. Both the 3d subshell and the 4s orbital are completely filled with paired electrons, so it has no unpaired electron.
